sections.h2: Who sets values and sends the bill
sections.html:
Springfield's A.B. Graham Building, 31 North Limestone Street, is home to both offices behind your tax bill. The auditor, at 937-521-1860, puts a value on each parcel. The treasurer, at 937-521-1832, prints and mails the bills and collects payment. Annual collections run about $135 million in real estate tax and $275,000 in manufactured home tax, and every bill stacks levies from several local taxing bodies.

To see which levies apply in your district, request the yearly rate sheet. It is linked on the property tax page, and the counter keeps paper copies. Send anything in writing, a new mailing address for example, to P.O. Box 1305, Springfield, OH 45501-1305. The treasurer's main page links to online payment.

The auditor works on a six year reappraisal cycle and does a sales-driven triennial update midway. A full reappraisal includes an inspection of each property, while an update looks only at sales. The 2022 round used 2019, 2020 and 2021 sales, valuing each home as of January 1, 2022.

A hired contractor runs a mass appraisal across more than 50,000 residential parcels. Location, lot size, age, style, square footage, construction quality, foundation, outbuildings and condition all feed into a value. Then the math: appraised value, then 35 percent of it, then the voted levies, gives the gross tax. Most rates are adjusted each year so every levy raises what it raised the year before.

A year's tax is split into two installments, one due in late February and one in early August, with exact dates printed on the bill. Mailing goes out 20 to 25 days before each deadline. Not receiving the bill is no defense against the tax or the penalties.

Penalty and interest steps in a typical Clark County year
WhenCharge
From the day after the first-half deadline to March 95% penalty on the unpaid current half
March 1010% penalty on the unpaid current half
From the day after the second-half deadline to August 175% penalty on everything still unpaid, real estate and manufactured home
August 1810% penalty on that same balance
September 15.83% interest on delinquent taxes from earlier years
December 11.17% interest on all unpaid real estate and manufactured home tax

Mailing a check close to the deadline has a catch. Under section 323.12 only a Postal Service postmark dated by the last day counts. A stamp from a private postage meter does not.

If a lump sum is hard to swing, join the treasurer's escrow program, which splits each half-year bill into equal monthly prepayments at no cost. After you sign an agreement, coupons arrive showing an estimate, though any amount on any day is accepted. Cash, check, money order and ACH debit are accepted.

  • Mail the Escrow Program Form to P.O. Box 1305, Springfield, OH 45501-1305, or email it to treasurer@clarkcountyohio.gov.
  • Any shortfall left by your prepayments is still due on the normal deadline, with the late penalty if missed.
  • Tell the office about a new mailing address in writing, because a bill mailed to your old address still counts.

Before listing, ask the treasurer what happens to a prepaid balance at closing.

Complaint forms are filed with the county auditor. The deadline in section 5715.19 is March 31 after the tax year, or the last day of first-half collection if that is later. Mailed forms are dated by postmark. The owner, a spouse or certain retained professionals may sign.

  • Each complaint is passed to the Clark County Board of Revision, which gets 180 days past the filing deadline to hear and rule.
  • You carry the burden. The strongest evidence is a recent arm's length sale, of your own house or a close match.
  • Pending the decision, you may send in tax on your claimed value and the treasurer must take it.
  • You get one complaint per interim period, unless circumstances changed afterward, for instance a sale, a casualty loss or a major addition.

Try the auditor's informal review first. Section 5715.19(G) obliges a complainant to hand the Board of Revision all the evidence they hold, and evidence kept back can be barred later at the Board of Tax Appeals or common pleas court without good cause.

The homestead credit goes to people 65 and over, owners with a permanent and total disability, and certain surviving spouses. For tax year 2026 it erases the tax on $29,700 of value if income is at or under $41,000. Disabled former service members receive the tax on $59,400 of value with no income test.

  • File Form DTE 105A (DTE 105I for disabled former service members), filed with the Clark County Auditor by December 31 of the credit year.
  • You must turn 65 by year end and have owned and occupied the home since January 1.
  • If denied, appeal to the Board of Revision on DTE 106B within 60 days.

County commissioners may add a matching local option under House Bill 96, signed in June 2025. The auditor can tell you if Clark County has one. A seller who qualifies should confirm the exemption is on file before listing, because the buyer's title agent will ask about it at closing.

Taxes owed stay attached to the parcel, so the title search turns them up. Phone 937-521-1832 for a payoff figure, give it to the closing agent, and let it be paid from your sale proceeds. Penalty and interest keep growing on the schedule above until the day of payment, so a payoff quote is only good for the day it is given. Ask the treasurer for the exact amount as close to closing as you can.

The deed adds a tax question of its own. Section 319.202 has the buyer record what the seller reports about whether current or prior year taxes will be reduced under homestead or owner-occupancy rules. Know your own answer before closing day, because a yes means a sworn estimate of the reduction travels with the deed. A cash sale skips lender underwriting, but the payoff and the deed statement are the same.

Springfield is the seat of Clark County, a 403 square mile stretch of west central Ohio. Only two cities exist, Springfield and New Carlisle, and 25.4 percent of 2020 residents lived in rural areas. The county has 55,975 households averaging 2.37 people. The median owner-occupied home is worth $169,900, and monthly owner costs run $1,262 with a mortgage and $523 without.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Clark County Treasurer?
faqs.a: Call 937-521-1832 for bill questions. The office is in the Graham Building on North Limestone Street in Springfield.

faqs.q: When are Clark County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due in late February and the second in early August. A 5 percent penalty and then a 10 percent penalty follow each deadline, so rely on the dates printed on your bill.

faqs.q: Who receives a Clark County valuation complaint?
faqs.a: The Clark County Auditor receives it and passes it to the Board of Revision. March 31 of the next year is the cutoff, unless first-half collection closes later.

faqs.q: Is there a way to pay Clark County tax monthly?
faqs.a: Yes, through the treasurer's escrow program, which charges nothing. Send the Escrow Program Form to P.O. Box 1305, Springfield.

faqs.q: How is a Clark County bill calculated from market value?
faqs.a: The auditor takes 35 percent of the appraised value and applies the voted levies to reach the gross tax. Credits come off after that.
